Laura / Karthik,

Summary: BrightScale sent redlined MSA + Order Form notes (attached). They call out SecureCloud Partners as the log processor. Procurement wants to close this week; BrightScale asked what evidence would be sufficient.

Questions for Legal / Contracts:
- Do we require a formal flow-down clause in the MSA or is an Order Form Annex sufficient when the subprocessor only handles logs?
- If we require consent, do we: (A) require prior written consent for each subprocessor, (B) accept an Annex listing subprocessors (Order Form amendment), or (C) accept evidence (signed DPA + SOC2) without an explicit consent clause?
- Any mandatory audit language or breach-notification tweaks we should push?

Constraints: BrightScale wants minimal changes to the MSA; they are okay with an Order Form amendment or an addendum. They will route PO after legal sign-off.

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Internal: BrightScale MSA/order form redlines — subproc pathing (please advise)

Aisha / Karthik —

Quick read and recommendations:

1) Preferred approach: Order Form Annex that enumerates the subprocessor(s) + short flow-down clause. Rationale: keeps MSA intact, fits BrightScale's ask for minimal MSA edits, and gives us a single amendable place to list processors.

Suggested annex language (short form):
"Annex X — Subprocessors: Customer acknowledges and agrees that Redwood may engage the listed subprocessors to perform Services. Redwood shall ensure that each subprocessor is subject to written data protection obligations no less protective than those in the DPA between the parties. Customer shall be notified of material changes to the subprocessor list and may request information (e.g., SOC2 Type II) for each listed subprocessor."

2) Evidence: Require either (i) SecureCloud to sign Redwood's DPA (preferred), or (ii) provide an equivalent signed DPA plus current SOC2 Type II report or SOC2 summary + ISO27001 cert. For expedited procurement, accept a notarized SOC2 summary plus an executed DPA, with a condition that the full SOC2 report be provided within 30 days.

3) Audits & breach language: Keep our standard audit rights scoped to the subprocessor if the customer asks. For this engagement, recommend we limit customer audit rights to review of evidence delivered by SecureCloud (SOC2 summary + DPA) rather than on-site audits.

4) Commercial / timing: No changes to pricing are required. If BrightScale insists on additional indemnities or unusual SLAs tied to the subprocessor, escalate for commercial review.

Action items for Aisha:
- Confirm with BrightScale that Annex X is acceptable.
- Request SecureCloud's SOC2 summary and executed DPA (or sign-off on Redwood DPA).
- If BrightScale prefers the MSA edited instead, we can provide tracked changes but that will take longer.

I'll draft a short Annex X and a one-paragraph email template to send to SecureCloud requesting evidence (SOC2 summary + signed DPA). I can have these to you by EOD Nov 2.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
